R549.note: Adding a @Configuration class with @EnableMethodSecurity is the correct, additive way to make the existing @PreAuthorize('hasRole(ADMIN)') guards enforce; the codebase-wide activation is stated and blocks nothing legitimate.

R550.note: execFile with an argument array plus '--' closes shell and flag injection, but the added multi-label domain regex rejects inputs the original endpoint accepted (single-label names, TLD-only queries like 'com', Unicode IDNs that whois handles natively), and the hard-coded /usr/bin/whois path is an assumption about the host layout.

R551.note: Magic-byte detection replaces the client Content-Type gate and the file is stored under a server-generated UUID with a fixed .png/.jpg extension, which is exactly what the stated contract asks for; both files in the store() call chain are updated consistently.

R552.note: Fixed '%s' format string with Encode.forHtml(param) closes both the reflected XSS and the format-string hazard; the loss of format-directive interpretation on the Referer is the vulnerability itself and is stated (obj is now unused rather than 'untouched', a cosmetic inaccuracy).

R553.note: htmlspecialchars with ENT_QUOTES|ENT_SUBSTITUTE|ENT_HTML5 and explicit UTF-8 at both concatenation points is the right encoder for HTML text context; ENT_SUBSTITUTE behaviour on invalid UTF-8 is stated and only affects malformed input.

R554.note: Replacing CSharpScript with DynamicExpresso.Interpreter exposing only Total and Tax (reflection left disabled) removes the compiler sink entirely, keeps the Task<object?> signature and JSON shape per the contract, and the write-up reports a live check of both a legitimate formula and blocked payloads.

R555.note: The [A-Za-z0-9]+ fullmatch (matching the docstring's stated 'short alphanumeric report key') is what closes the vector; the write-up's claim that the list form under shell=True is an independent second layer is wrong - reproduced in a scratch dir with Python 3.13: Popen([bat, 'abc&dir>marker2.txt'], shell=True) executed the injected command because list2cmdline only quotes args containing whitespace.

R556.note: htmlspecialchars(ENT_QUOTES, UTF-8) applied at every echo of request-derived data, including the flagged $_POST['note'] and the sibling $_GET reflections, with no change to accepted input.

R557.note: The regex excludes CR/LF and '>' so the RCPT TO line cannot be broken out of, but it is a character allowlist that rejects legitimate RFC 5321 addresses the original accepted (apostrophe and other atext characters in the local part, quoted local parts, IP-literal domains), and the write-up claims it rejects only impossible addresses.

R558.note: Binding the RSA public key to RS256 via new Key(...) on php-jwt >= 6.0 is the correct fix for the key-confusion bypass; dropping HS256 removes no working path because the original only ever verified HS256 against the public key, and the manifest bump and narrowing are stated plainly.

R559.note: escapeshellarg() is the correct sink-level API for shell_exec and closes the metacharacter injection; no '--' is added so a leading-dash host reaches ping as an option, but as the sole remaining argument it cannot supply a destination and ping just fails with usage, so this is not exploitable here.

R560.note: Backslash-hex escaping of the five RFC 4515 filter metacharacters before concatenation into (uid=...) closes the injection while preserving the query shape; the added string/non-empty check only rejects a missing or array username, which was never a legitimate lookup, and is stated.
